title.sl: Odvisni govor: she said she was
title.de: Indirekte Rede: she said she was
title.it: Il discorso indiretto: she said she was

goal.sl: Poveš, kaj je kdo rekel (She said she was tired), ločiš say in tell, premakneš čas, kraj in dan ter poveš, kaj ti je kdo naročil (She told me to wait).
goal.de: Du sagst, was jemand gesagt hat (She said she was tired), unterscheidest say und tell, verschiebst Zeit, Ort und Tag und sagst, was man dir aufgetragen hat (She told me to wait).
goal.it: Riferisci ciò che qualcuno ha detto (She said she was tired), distingui say e tell, sposti tempo, luogo e giorno e dici che cosa ti è stato chiesto di fare (She told me to wait).
goal.en: You can report what someone said (She said she was tired), tell say from tell, shift the tense, the place and the day, and say what you were told to do (She told me to wait).

say.sl: Kaj je kdo rekel: **said** + stavek, čas gre korak nazaj: **am, is → was**. »I'm tired.« → **She said she was tired.** (Rekla je, da je utrujena.) **that** lahko izpustiš: **She said that she was tired.** Slovenščina ostane v sedanjiku, angleščina ne: **are → were**: **They said they were late.** (Rekli so, da zamujajo.)
say.de: Was jemand gesagt hat: **said** + Satz, die Zeit geht einen Schritt zurück: **am, is → was**. „I'm tired.“ → **She said she was tired.** (Sie sagte, sie sei müde.) **that** kannst du weglassen: **She said that she was tired.** Deutsch nimmt den Konjunktiv, Englisch geht zurück: **are → were**: **They said they were late.** (Sie sagten, sie seien spät dran.)
say.it: Ciò che qualcuno ha detto: **said** + una frase, il tempo fa un passo indietro: **am, is → was**. «I'm tired.» → **She said she was tired.** (Ha detto che era stanca.) **that** si può togliere: **She said that she was tired.** Anche **are → were**: **They said they were late.** (Hanno detto che erano in ritardo.)
say.en: What someone said: **said** + a sentence, the tense goes one step back: **am, is → was**. “I'm tired.” → **She said she was tired.** You can leave out **that**: **She said that she was tired.** And **are → were**: **They said they were late.**

examples.en: She said that she was tired.
examples.de: Sie sagte, dass sie müde sei.
Sie sagten, sie seien spät dran.
examples.it: Hanno detto che erano in ritardo.

ask.text: “I'm cold,” said Edna. → Edna said she ___ cold.

explain.sl:
**Čas korak nazaj**
- Edna said she was cold.
explain.de:
**Die Zeit einen Schritt zurück**
- Edna said she was cold.
explain.it:
**Il tempo un passo indietro**
- Edna said she was cold.
explain.en:
**The tense one step back**
- Edna said she was cold.

say.sl: **say** + kaj, **tell** + komu: **She said she was tired.** **She told me she was tired.** (Povedala mi je, da je utrujena.) Pri tell navadno stoji, komu: **He told us a story.** (Povedal nam je zgodbo.) **said to me** je tudi prav. *She said me* in *She told to me* sta napaki.
say.de: **say** + was, **tell** + wem: **She said she was tired.** **She told me she was tired.** (Sie sagte mir, sie sei müde.) Bei tell steht meist, wem: **He told us a story.** (Er erzählte uns eine Geschichte.) **said to me** ist auch richtig. *She said me* und *She told to me* sind Fehler.
say.it: **say** + che cosa, **tell** + a chi: **She said she was tired.** **She told me she was tired.** (Mi ha detto che era stanca.) Con tell di solito c'è a chi: **He told us a story.** (Ci ha raccontato una storia.) **said to me** è anche giusto. *She said me* e *She told to me* sono errori.
say.en: **say** + what, **tell** + who: **She said she was tired.** **She told me she was tired.** With tell there's usually a who: **He told us a story.** **said to me** is right too. *She said me* and *She told to me* are mistakes.

examples.en: She told me she was tired.
examples.sl: Povedala mi je, da je utrujena.
examples.de: Sie sagte mir, sie sei müde.
examples.it: Mi ha detto che era stanca.

examples.en: She said to me she was tired.
examples.sl: Rekla mi je, da je utrujena.
examples.de: Sie sagte zu mir, sie sei müde.
examples.it: Mi ha detto che era stanca.

explain.it:

say.sl: Še drugi koraki nazaj: **will → would**, **can → could**, **am going to → was going to**, **don't → didn't**. **He said he would come.** (Rekel je, da bo prišel.) **She said she could help.** (Rekla je, da lahko pomaga.) Preteklik: »I saw a raven.« → **He said he had seen a raven.** (Rekel je, da je videl krokarja.) Tudi **he saw a raven** je prav.
say.de: Noch mehr Schritte zurück: **will → would**, **can → could**, **am going to → was going to**, **don't → didn't**. **He said he would come.** (Er sagte, er würde kommen.) **She said she could help.** (Sie sagte, sie könne helfen.) Die Vergangenheit: „I saw a raven.“ → **He said he had seen a raven.** (Er sagte, er habe einen Raben gesehen.) Auch **he saw a raven** ist richtig.
say.it: Altri passi indietro: **will → would**, **can → could**, **am going to → was going to**, **don't → didn't**. **He said he would come.** (Ha detto che sarebbe venuto.) **She said she could help.** (Ha detto che poteva aiutare.) Il passato: «I saw a raven.» → **He said he had seen a raven.** (Ha detto che aveva visto un corvo.) Anche **he saw a raven** è giusto.
say.en: More steps back: **will → would**, **can → could**, **am going to → was going to**, **don't → didn't**. **He said he would come.** **She said she could help.** The past: “I saw a raven.” → **He said he had seen a raven.** **he saw a raven** is right too.

examples.en: He said he had seen a raven.
examples.sl: Rekel je, da je videl krokarja.
examples.de: Er sagte, er habe einen Raben gesehen.
examples.it: Ha detto che aveva visto un corvo.

ask.text: “I will come,” said Jack. → Jack said he ___ come.

explain.sl:
**Čas korak nazaj**
- Jack said he would come.
explain.de:
**Die Zeit einen Schritt zurück**
- Jack said he would come.
explain.it:
**Il tempo un passo indietro**
- Jack said he would come.
explain.en:
**The tense one step back**
- Jack said he would come.

say.sl: Če je še vedno res, ljudje čas pogosto pustijo: **She said she's tired.** (Rekla je, da je utrujena.) **Jack said he'll come.** (Jack je rekel, da bo prišel.) Tudi to je prav. Korak nazaj je vedno prav in pri pisanju najbolj varen: **She said she was tired.**
say.de: Wenn es noch stimmt, lassen die Leute die Zeit oft: **She said she's tired.** (Sie sagte, sie sei müde.) **Jack said he'll come.** (Jack sagte, er komme.) Auch das ist richtig. Der Schritt zurück ist immer richtig und beim Schreiben der sichere Weg: **She said she was tired.**
say.it: Se è ancora vero, spesso il tempo resta: **She said she's tired.** (Ha detto che è stanca.) **Jack said he'll come.** (Jack ha detto che verrà.) Anche questo è giusto. Il passo indietro è sempre giusto, e scrivendo è la scelta più sicura: **She said she was tired.**
say.en: If it's still so, people often keep the tense: **She said she's tired.** **Jack said he'll come.** That's right too. The step back is always right, and the safe choice in writing: **She said she was tired.**

examples.sl: Jack je rekel, da bo prišel.

say.sl: Zamenjaj osebo in besede za kraj in čas: **I → she**, **my → her**, **here → there**, **today → that day**, **tomorrow → the next day**, **yesterday → the day before**. »I'll come here tomorrow.« → **She said she'd come there the next day.** (Rekla je, da bo prišla tja naslednji dan.) Če si še vedno tam in je še isti dan, besede ostanejo.
say.de: Wechsle die Person und die Wörter für Ort und Zeit: **I → she**, **my → her**, **here → there**, **today → that day**, **tomorrow → the next day**, **yesterday → the day before**. „I'll come here tomorrow.“ → **She said she'd come there the next day.** (Sie sagte, sie werde am nächsten Tag dorthin kommen.) Bist du noch dort und ist es noch derselbe Tag, bleiben die Wörter.
say.it: Cambia la persona e le parole di luogo e tempo: **I → she**, **my → her**, **here → there**, **today → that day**, **tomorrow → the next day**, **yesterday → the day before**. «I'll come here tomorrow.» → **She said she'd come there the next day.** (Ha detto che sarebbe venuta lì il giorno dopo.) Se sei ancora lì ed è lo stesso giorno, le parole restano.
say.en: Change the person and the words for place and time: **I → she**, **my → her**, **here → there**, **today → that day**, **tomorrow → the next day**, **yesterday → the day before**. “I'll come here tomorrow.” → **She said she'd come there the next day.** If you're still there and it's still the same day, the words stay.

examples.en: She said she'd come there the next day.
examples.sl: Rekla je, da bo prišla tja naslednji dan.
examples.de: Sie sagte, sie werde am nächsten Tag dorthin kommen.
examples.it: Ha detto che sarebbe venuta lì il giorno dopo.

examples.en: He said he had seen her the day before.
examples.sl: Rekel je, da jo je videl dan prej.
examples.de: Er sagte, er habe sie am Tag davor gesehen.
examples.it: Ha detto che l'aveva vista il giorno prima.

ask.text: On Monday Jack said, “I'll come tomorrow.” → He said he'd come ___.

explain.sl:
**Kraj in čas se premakneta**
- He said he'd come the next day.
explain.de:
**Ort und Zeit wechseln**
- He said he'd come the next day.
explain.it:
**Luogo e tempo cambiano**
- He said he'd come the next day.
explain.en:

say.sl: Ukaz: **told me to** + osnovna oblika: »Wait here.« → **She told me to wait there.** (Rekla mi je, naj tam počakam.) **told me not to**: **Jack told me not to feed the dog.** (Jack mi je rekel, naj ne hranim psa.) Prošnja: **She asked me to wait.** (Prosila me je, naj počakam.)
say.de: Befehl: **told me to** + Grundform: „Wait here.“ → **She told me to wait there.** (Sie sagte mir, ich solle dort warten.) **told me not to**: **Jack told me not to feed the dog.** (Jack sagte mir, ich solle den Hund nicht füttern.) Bitte: **She asked me to wait.** (Sie bat mich zu warten.)
say.it: Un ordine: **told me to** + la forma base: «Wait here.» → **She told me to wait there.** (Mi ha detto di aspettare lì.) **told me not to**: **Jack told me not to feed the dog.** (Jack mi ha detto di non dare da mangiare al cane.) Una richiesta: **She asked me to wait.** (Mi ha chiesto di aspettare.)
say.en: An order: **told me to** + the base form: “Wait here.” → **She told me to wait there.** **told me not to**: **Jack told me not to feed the dog.** A request: **She asked me to wait.**

examples.en: She told me to wait there.
examples.sl: Rekla mi je, naj tam počakam.
examples.de: Sie sagte mir, ich solle dort warten.
examples.it: Mi ha detto di aspettare lì.

examples.en: Jack told me not to feed the dog.
examples.sl: Jack mi je rekel, naj ne hranim psa.
examples.de: Jack sagte mir, ich solle den Hund nicht füttern.
examples.it: Jack mi ha detto di non dare da mangiare al cane.

exercises.text: — I saw Sam last month. He ___ me he ___ (be) tired. He said he ___ (can, not) sleep. — What else did he ___? — He said he ___ (sell) the van the next week. He ___ me not to tell you. — And what did you ___ him? — I told him I ___ (not say) a word!

translation.sl: — Prejšnji mesec sem {m:videl|f:videla} Sama. Povedal mi je, da je utrujen. Rekel je, da ne more spati. — Kaj je še rekel? — Rekel je, da bo naslednji teden prodal kombi. Rekel mi je, naj ti ne povem. — In kaj si mu {m:rekel|f:rekla}? — {m:Rekel|f:Rekla} sem mu, da ne bom {m:črhnil|f:črhnila} niti besede!
translation.de: — Ich habe letzten Monat Sam gesehen. Er sagte mir, er sei müde. Er sagte, er könne nicht schlafen. — Was hat er noch gesagt? — Er sagte, er werde den Lieferwagen in der nächsten Woche verkaufen. Er sagte mir, ich solle es dir nicht sagen. — Und was hast du ihm gesagt? — Ich sagte ihm, ich würde kein Wort sagen!
translation.it: — Il mese scorso ho visto Sam. Mi ha detto che era stanco. Ha detto che non riusciva a dormire. — Che altro ha detto? — Ha detto che avrebbe venduto il furgone la settimana dopo. Mi ha detto di non dirtelo. — E tu che cosa gli hai detto? — Gli ho detto che non avrei detto una parola!
translation.en: — I saw Sam last month. He told me he was tired. He said he couldn't sleep. — What else did he say? — He said he would sell the van the next week. He told me not to tell you. — And what did you tell him? — I told him I wouldn't say a word!
